lab_title: AR Human Heart Anatomy and Blood Flow
top_level_objectives: Identify the major anatomical structures of the human heart, including chambers, valves, and associated major blood vessels.
Trace the path of blood through both pulmonary and systemic circulation loops, identifying the sequence of structures involved.
Explain the functional significance of myocardial thickness in the ventricles and the role of heart valves in preventing backflow.

scenes.brief_purpose: Introduce the heart's position within the thoracic cavity and observe its external features.
key_visuals: A realistic 3D model of the human torso with a partially transparent rib cage and lungs, revealing the heart in anatomical position.
External anterior view of the heart model, highlighting major external sulci and great vessels.
student_actions: Rotate and zoom the torso model to observe the heart's location relative to other organs.
Identify the mediastinum as the region containing the heart.
Observe the general external shape and orientation of the heart.

scenes.brief_purpose: Explore the internal structure of the heart, focusing on identifying the four chambers.
key_visuals: A cutaway 3D model of the heart, revealing the internal chambers.
Labels highlighting the right atrium, right ventricle, left atrium, and left ventricle.
student_actions: Select and highlight each of the four heart chambers to identify them individually.
Observe the relative sizes and locations of the atria and ventricles.
Examine the septa dividing the atria and ventricles.

scenes.brief_purpose: Identify the four heart valves and the major blood vessels entering and leaving the heart, understanding their connections.
key_visuals: The cutaway heart model with emphasis on the tricuspid, pulmonary, mitral (bicuspid), and aortic valves.
Major blood vessels (superior and inferior vena cava, pulmonary arteries, pulmonary veins, aorta) clearly visible and distinctly colored to indicate oxygenation status.
student_actions: Tap to identify each of the four heart valves and learn its specific name.
Trace the connection of major vessels to their respective heart chambers (e.g., vena cava to right atrium, aorta from left ventricle).
Observe the structure of the valves, noting the presence of cusps or leaflets.

scenes.brief_purpose: Trace the path of deoxygenated blood from the body, through the right side of the heart, and to the lungs.
key_visuals: Animated blood flow (blue to represent deoxygenated blood) moving through the vena cava, right atrium, tricuspid valve, right ventricle, pulmonary valve, and into the pulmonary arteries.
A schematic representation of the lungs as the destination for pulmonary circulation.
student_actions: Initiate and follow the animated path of deoxygenated blood through the right side of the heart.
Identify and name each structure the blood passes through in sequence during pulmonary circulation.
Explain the role of the tricuspid and pulmonary valves in this pathway.

scenes.brief_purpose: Trace the path of oxygenated blood from the lungs, through the left side of the heart, and out to the body.
key_visuals: Animated blood flow (red to represent oxygenated blood) moving from the pulmonary veins, left atrium, mitral valve, left ventricle, aortic valve, and into the aorta.
A schematic representation of the body's tissues as the destination for systemic circulation.
student_actions: Initiate and follow the animated path of oxygenated blood through the left side of the heart.
Identify and name each structure the blood passes through in sequence during systemic circulation.
Explain the role of the mitral and aortic valves in this pathway.

scenes.scene_name: Cardiac Mechanics: Ventricle Walls and Valves
scenes.brief_purpose: Understand the functional difference in ventricular myocardial thickness and observe how heart valves prevent backflow.
key_visuals: A detailed cross-section of the ventricles, explicitly comparing the myocardial thickness of the left and right ventricular walls.
An animation demonstrating the opening and closing of a chosen heart valve (e.g., mitral valve), showing how it prevents backflow during ventricular contraction.
student_actions: Compare and contrast the wall thickness of the left and right ventricles, considering their respective functions.
Activate an animation to visualize the coordinated opening and closing of heart valves.
Describe how the structure of the valves contributes to unidirectional blood flow and prevents regurgitation.
